statements.status_notes: Backported the upstream Storable SX_HOOK I32_MAX guard from Perl commit e4f681784bcdeaa91ff02a2fa4cdcae5c46779d7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package rejects an SX_HOOK item count of I32_MAX before calling av_extend, so the signed overflow panic during thaw/retrieve is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream S_measure_struct overflow guards from Perl commits 5f7eb6bbbe0510964e3fb1d6bb691e5445913e55 and 40754edc72dd3e513d758153c0e2f0215897740e into the DHI perl package. The patched package croaks when a pack/unpack structure size would overflow SSize_t and uses overflow-safe bit/nibble length math, so the out-of-bounds heap read is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream Perl_study_chunk trie overflow guard from Perl commit 03f74bbbd3a68350d926ee93d56ee4808c28c4c7 into the DHI perl package. The patched package skips trie optimization when the start-to-tail delta would overflow a 16-bit field, so the silently incorrect match behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream HTTP::Tiny 0.095 credentialed-redirect hardening (allow_credentialed_redirects / allow_downgrade defaults, plus protocol-relative Location handling) into the bundled HTTP::Tiny shipped by the DHI perl package. The patched HTTP::Tiny strips caller-supplied Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization headers on cross-origin redirects and refuses https-to-http redirects by default, so the credential-forwarding behavior is mitigated inline.

Memory leak in the xmllint interactive shell when the input line contains only whitespace. The DHI libxml2 APK backports the upstream fix for rebuilt r2 (3.23) and r3 (3.24) releases; stock Alpine PURLs remain under investigation until consumers pick up the DHI rebuild. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-1757

Stack buffer overflows in the xmlcatalog interactive shell (--shell) usershell() parser in upstream Alpine libxml2 2.13.9 packages. The DHI libxml2 APK backports the upstream fix for rebuilt r2 (3.23) and r3 (3.24) releases; stock Alpine PURLs remain under investigation until consumers pick up the DHI rebuild.

CVE-2026-0989 is uncontrolled recursion in the RelaxNG external-schema inclusion parser, fixed upstream in libxml2 2.15.2. Alpine 3.x ships libxml2 2.13.9; backporting the RelaxNG recursion-depth fix to 2.13.x is not practical. DHI catalog images use libxml2 as a general-purpose XML library and do not document RelaxNG schema validation on untrusted RelaxNG inputs as a supported runtime path.

Uncontrolled recursion in xmlParseSGMLCatalog is reachable only when a local user parses an untrusted SGML catalog with the xmlcatalog CLI. Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible. The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the 2.13.x source without invasive changes for a negligible CLI-only issue. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-8732

statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

This is an out-of-memory denial-of-service issue in TIFFReadEncodedStrip(). Debian treats it as unimportant with negligible security impact when applications follow the documented memory-allocation guidance, including TIFFOpenOptionsSetMaxSingleMemAlloc(). There is no upstream fix available to backport.
This is a tiff2ps CLI crash with no practical security impact for the DHI package. Debian marks the issue as minor/no-dsa, and there is no upstream fix available to backport.

This is a tiff2pdf crash through ijg-libjpeg behavior rather than a libtiff library flaw, and the Debian security tracker treats it as unimportant. The DHI package does not expose this CLI crash as a security boundary.

The original report has not been confirmed by the reporter after repeated attempts, third parties reported being unable to reproduce it, and SUSE analysis indicates the report is likely a duplicate of CVE-2017-9935. The DHI package treats this as a non-issue unless a reproducible upstream report becomes available.

The related upstream fix, commit 25f9ffa56548c1846c4a1f19308b7f561f7b1ab0, was included upstream before libtiff 4.0.9 and is present in the 4.7.0 Debian source used by the DHI package. The remaining memory-based denial-of-service behavior is not planned for a complete upstream fix and is not treated as a security-impacting issue for this package.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
